What a /30 means

A /30 leaves exactly two usable addresses, which made it the traditional choice for point-to-point links.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /30 uses 30 network bits and leaves 2 host bits, so the block contains 4 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−30) − 2 = 4 − 2 = 2.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.252
!
access-list 10 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.3

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 192.168.1.1/30

Linux

ip addr add 192.168.1.1/30 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /30?

2. A /30 has 4 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 2 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /30?

255.255.255.252. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.0.0.3.
